mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during a quarter with a >0.5% FEDFUNDS increase, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during periods when GDPC1 declines YoY, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during two consecutive months with UNRATE > 6.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, lowering earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during any 3-month window of INDPRO decline, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average
failure_condition: If, in periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If, during months with a >10% drop in HOUST, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE signals a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: If, during periods with rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows YoY for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If, during any 3-month window with YoY RSAFS growth, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.
